newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BBA won't bid on Banerj sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BBA won't bid on Banerj sell-off.

text.p: Brazilian private bank Banco BBA Creditanstalt said it will not participate in the privatization auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj and its insurer next Tuesday.

Banco BBA, which had prequalified to bid on the Banerj sell-off, declined to give further details, but the bank's president Fernao Bracher has told reporters BBA considered Banerj's minimum price too high.

Banerj and its insurance company will be sold off for a minimum price of 436.693 million reais and 43.310 million reais, respectively, at a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange (BVRJ).
Investors are required to purchase the bank and the insurer together.
Banco BBA is currently holding talks to acquire a controlling stake in local bank BCN, which may have contributed to lead the bank to drop out of the running, analysts said.
On Thursday prequalified bidder Bank of Boston Corp's Brazil unit had announced its decision to drop out of Banerj's sell-off.

Newspapers said other three of the eight prequalified bidders -- Banco CCF do Brasil, Companhia de Investimentos Latino-Americana and health insurance firm Golden Cross -- also have given up to take part in the auction.
So far General Electric Co's General Electric Capital Corporation, Banco Itau and Bradesco appear to be bidding on Banerj's sale.

The fact that investors have dropped out of the bank's sell-off is not a concern, said Paulo Ferraz, president of private bank Bozano, Simonsen, which managed Banerj this year and prepared it for privatization.
"I think there will be competition," Ferraz said.
